claims.statement: app-lynx routing runs the official vue-router on createMemoryHistory(); the app has no URL-based routing, and the single flat `routes` array in `packages/app-lynx/src/router.ts` is the entire navigation surface (29 route records, asserted as such by the integration test).

Per-route behaviour is declared in vue-router `meta` through a module augmentation that is the single declaration site: `requiresAuth` (optional boolean), `backBehavior: 'exit'` (optional), and `topInset: TopInsetMode` which is deliberately REQUIRED with no default so a forgotten declaration fails `vue-tsc` instead of silently falling back; unknown inset modes normalize to 'self' with a one-time warning.

The auth marking rule is asymmetric on purpose: `/update` and `/error` carry `backBehavior: 'exit'` and no `requiresAuth` because they are the destination of flows that first clear the session (forced update, 401 expiry), so marking them would make the guard redirect its own destination; `/login`, `/network-check` and `/platform-check` are also unmarked, and every other route is `requiresAuth: true`.

The four top-level destinations are discover / updates / shelf / me, answering four different user questions (ADR-0218 dimension split); `/illusts` and `/novels` keep their route records (deep links, benchNav, back targets) but were demoted out of navigation into in-page tabs of the discover page, and the debug/self-check items moved from Me into the secondary page `/advanced`.

The navigation dimension split carries a one-time migration notice owned by `stores/navMigrationNotice.ts`: its seen flag is a device-level key with no uid suffix (`nav_migration_v1_seen`) and is deliberately outside the backup domain, dismiss writes the flag to disk before flipping memory, and a read failure resolves to 'not seen yet' with a warning rather than permanently silencing the notice.

Because memory history starts at 'nowhere', the router is anchored at module load by `router.replace(DISCOVER_PATH)` with `DISCOVER_PATH = '/discover'`; replace rather than push matters because a push-anchored start would leave the nowhere entry behind as a phantom previous page that the queue probe would report as a valid back target.

`initRouter()` is the shell bootstrap sequence: it registers the unauthorized handler and the session-error handler (which clears history and replaces to /error), registers the system-back handler on native, restores the token, loads settings, fires non-blocking hydrations for watchLater / continueReading / browsingHistory so deep links do not render 'you have nothing', runs the startup auto-backup after settings are loaded, performs the initial `navigate(ok ? '/discover' : '/login', { replace: true })`, and only then calls `markBootstrapDone()`.

`afterEach` replaces `routeState` wholesale with `{ name, path, params, topInset }` (topInset written in the same batch as name/params so the inset owner never lags a frame) and commits the pending transition direction in the same microtask, which is before Vue's render flush — that ordering is what gives the incoming page an animated first frame; the intent is reconciled against the actual landing path so a cancelled or guard-redirected navigation gets direction `none`.

`routeState`'s initial value is a placeholder whose path already equals the first real landing route (`/discover`, topInset 'self'), so consumers that must observe every landing — such as the top-level reach metric in `App.vue` — watch the whole `routeState.value` object; watching `.path` would compare /discover with /discover at cold start and never fire.

The auth gate is the pure function `decideRequiresAuth(requiresAuth, bootstrapping, cleared, loggedIn)` wired into `router.beforeEach`: routes without `requiresAuth` always pass, the bootstrap window always passes (the guard must never await the network, or RouterView would render blank), and after `markBootstrapDone()` a cleared session or logged-out user navigating a protected route is redirected to `/login` with replace semantics.

`cleared` is a second session dimension independent of `isLoggedIn`: `resetHistory()` (logout, session expiry) sets it and physically empties the mirror stack, while `markSessionEstablished()` (login success, called from the login page) clears the flag and empties the mirror, so a re-login cannot reach a previous session's pages.

`hasBackEntry()` is a conjunction, not a query: it requires the session mirror stack to be non-empty AND `hasBackEntryIn(history)` to find a real previous entry. The probe silently moves the queue pointer with `history.go(-1, false)` and restores it with `go(1, false)`, which is synchronous, fires no listeners and keeps no state; the probe exists as a drift watchdog because memory history cannot be physically cleared.

`navigate()` records the previous path in the mirror only when the navigation actually landed where it was asked to (`currentRoute.fullPath === path && prev !== path`), so a push that a guard redirected to /login leaves no garbage mirror entry; an unresolvable path falls back to `replace('/login')`, preserving the pre-migration behaviour for unknown routes.

`goBack()` pops the mirror first and uses its top as the expected landing for transition reconciliation before calling `router.back()`; when the mirror and the real queue disagree, it clears the mirror and degrades to `replace('/discover')` with direction declared as `back`, so the drift path never leaves the user on a root route that claims a back entry exists.

System back is decided by the pure `evaluateBackRoute` in an ordered chain: an open modal wins first (close the top modal and stop), otherwise back guards run, otherwise `meta.backBehavior: 'exit'` / history / the double-tap exit window apply; `handleSystemBack` maps each action to `closeTopModal`, a no-op, `goBack()`, `PictelioApp.exitApp` or the exit hint.

Page-level back guards are a registry created by `createBackGuardRegistry`: guards run in registration order and short-circuit on the first `true`, a guard that throws is treated as NOT intercepting (fail-open with a console warning, so a buggy guard cannot wedge the back key), and `registerBackGuard` returns an idempotent unregister function for page unmount/deactivate.

`requestBack()` — the in-page back entry used by back buttons — shares the back-guard chain with the system-back bridge but deliberately does NOT consult the modal stack: only the system-back path closes an open sheet, so a page that both shows a sheet and draws a back button must route that button through the sheet's own close request.

The native system-back bridge is registered once and only in native mode: LynxActivity forwards a `pictelioBack` global event and JS decides everything; `exit` calls `PictelioApp.exitApp(cb)` with a mandatory callback (Lynx native-module convention), and at a root route a first back shows the `exitHint` capsule while a second back within `SYSTEM_BACK_EXIT_WINDOW_MS` (2000 ms) exits.

The KeepAlive route instance cache wraps the routed component with `:include="['discover', 'updates', 'shelf', 'me', 'ranking', 'mypixiv']"` and matches by component `name`, so each cached page declares `defineOptions({ name })` equal to its route name; detail pages are deliberately excluded because they load by `:id` and a cached instance would show the previous id's content.

Caching changes lifecycle semantics the shell must respect: pages inside `:include` mount once and get `onActivated` on re-entry (which is why the notification unread-badge refresh is wired in `onActivated`), and modules that key cleanup on `onUnmounted` break silently if their host is later added to `:include` — a precondition `composables/useImmersiveChrome.ts` documents for its own host.

Route transitions are built on the navigation side because Lynx has no router transition and no `transitionend`: `decideRouteDirection` maps `replace: true` to `none` and otherwise defaults to `forward`, `back` is declared explicitly by `goBack()`, and forward (slide from the right plus fade) is intentionally not the mirror image of back (slide from the left, no fade). Each direction has an `-alt` keyframe variant because the same animation name on the same element does not replay.

Carrying the transition `transform` on the wrapper makes it the containing block for `position: absolute` descendants for the duration of the entry animation, which would narrow in-page full-screen overlays to the content box; this is a registered, bounded trade-off because no full-screen overlay can be opened during a navigation and the timer removes the transform when it expires.

`createGlobalFab` derives two visibility values that must not be conflated: `routeMode` (menu for the four NAV_TABS routes, hidden for login/update/error, search for every other content route) and `mode`, which additionally collapses to `hidden` whenever a modal is open, plus a force-close of the menu; geometry consumers such as `FabAllowanceSpacer` must read `routeMode` because `mode` flips with sheet open/close and would make reserved content height jump.

The outer ring is a closed 4-item set sourced from `NAV_TABS`; a fifth destination is not a light change because the ring-item centre distance would fall below the 56 dp item diameter and force a larger radius plus device re-verification. Ring badges are injected through the `navBadge` dependency, only `updates` is wired (to `notificationStore.unreadCount`), and the value is prefetched at cold start in `App.vue` because without that prefetch the badge stays 0 unless the user happens to open Me.

The page→FAB bridge `usePage(routeName, actions)` is keyed by route name (KeepAlive-safe, returns an unregister function), and the active page is resolved by matching that name against NAV_TABS — so only registrations under the four tab route names take effect, while registrations under other route names are inert and those pages keep their own RefreshableList FAB. The inner ring is 'global search item first, then active page actions', and an empty registration yields a search-only inner ring.

Busy is an explicit mutual-exclusion dimension in the FAB: an in-flight refresh or async extra item sets busy (spinner, toggling disabled, other items no-op) while `select`, `close` and `search` stay allowed, page-action rejections are caught and warned instead of escaping to the UI, and back-to-top carries its own 1 s re-entry guard.

Native LynxView hit-testing ignores `pointer-events`, which constrains every floating layer in the shell: the FAB renders its scrim and rings behind `v-if="view.isOpen"` and keeps its outer container as a zero-size anchor pinned at (0,0) with children positioned by `left`/`top` in vw (Lynx resolves absolute positioning against the nearest view ancestor, not the viewport), and the shell's transient notices are capsule-positioned rather than full-width so they do not swallow taps.

The radial FAB is mounted outside KeepAlive in the shell and is suppressed entirely while a page owns immersive chrome, via the global `chromeSuppressed` flag that is derived from the single ownership token in `composables/useImmersiveChrome.ts` rather than from a second boolean.

ADR-0216 removed the visible header row from the four root pages without removing the top inset: all four still resolve their zero-content spacer through `composables/useTopInsetSpacer.ts` (per-page ownership per ADR-0214), and the `PICTELIO_HOME_BLEED` rollback valve now only flips the discover route's inset mode between bleed and self — it no longer restores the old header, and the route meta and page template branch must both derive from the same build-time macro.

Secondary pages keep a visible header through `components/PageTopBar.vue`, which owns two variants (centred title; back arrow + title + right `#action` slot), renders the self-mode spacer above the row itself, keeps one global height for both variants, and exposes `back` as an emitted event — the choice between `goBack()` and `requestBack()` belongs to the calling page.

The bottom side is asymmetric to the top on purpose: the root `<page>` keeps `paddingBottom: safeBottom` for ordinary page content, while the FAB allowance is no longer a global reserved band — it moved into each scrolling page's own content as a zero-content `FabAllowanceSpacer` at the end of the list, whose height follows route-derived FAB geometry, and which must be the last child of the scroll content and must not be wrapped in a conditional.

The modal stack (`stores/modalStack.ts`) is a LIFO registry of close callbacks: `registerModal(close)` returns an unregister function, `hasOpenModal()` answers the back-key question and `closeTopModal()` pops and invokes the topmost callback, which is what makes sheet-over-sheet behave as a stack for the system back key.

Bottom sheets are unmount-visible by necessity (pointer-events cannot hide them), so hosts control mounting with `v-if` and the shell components own no `open` state; both `BottomSheet.vue` and `SheetShell.vue` enforce the same hit-test structure — the root `absolute inset-0` layer is only a positioning context with no handler, the scrim is the full-screen interactive surface whose tap closes, the panel root stops propagation, and z-order comes from DOM order (scrim before panel), not `z-index`.

`components/SheetShell.vue` is the single definer of the repository's `sheet-*` and `dialog-*` keyframes (panel slide pair, scrim opacity pair and the non-bottom-anchored dialog scale pair), and its frame bodies contain only transform/opacity so durations and curves stay in `composables/motion.ts`.

Sheet dismissal is an explicit two-phase state machine implemented once in `composables/useSheetDismiss.ts` (`enter → exit → gone`) because Lynx has no `transitionend` and sheets are unmount-visible: a close request attaches the exit animation and starts a timer whose duration comes from the same `exit()` preset object's `holdMs`, repeated close requests are idempotent via `phase`, reduced motion degrades the preset to `none` with `holdMs` 0, and `dispose()` must clear the timer on unmount.

The global search sheet is a shell singleton: `App.vue` mounts exactly one `SearchSheet` behind `v-if="searchSheet.isOpen"`, and the store registers its close callback with the modal stack on open (unregistering on close) so the system back key closes it; all close paths (scrim, ×, result tap, back key) funnel through the store's close action, and unmounting resets the sheet state.

benchNav device-verification deep links are registered at module load, native-mode only, and only when the build-time `__BENCH_NAV__` flag is set (production eliminates the block): static scenarios map event names to routes and navigate with `replace` (idempotent under the native repeat-broadcast windows), user-scoped scenarios resolve the id from `authStore.currentUser` at event time and warn when logged out, and detail scenarios take a numeric payload and warn when it is missing or malformed.

benchNav correctness is cross-language: a parity test extracts every `pictelioBenchNav*` event name from `router.ts` and requires a matching dispatch literal in `LynxActivity.java`, because a scenario registered only on the JS side fails silently on device.

The notification click landing in the routing half is deliberately NOT gated by `__BENCH_NAV__` (it is product behaviour that must exist in release), dedupes by the native-generated `clickId` before counting, also pulls a pending click after subscribing because the four broadcast windows can all precede the JS subscription, and navigates to `/notifications` with `push` rather than `replace` so the back decision's session mirror stack agrees with the real queue.

A notification's `pixiv://` target_url is resolved by the pure resolver in `utils/notificationTarget.ts` (users → /user/:id, illusts → /illust/:id, novels → the novel entry point that can respect the intro-page setting) with http(s) sent to the system browser and everything else silently ignored; parsing is string-based because the Lynx URL polyfill does not provide a working hostname, so URL globals are banned.

The top-level reach metric is recorded at route landing, not at FAB dispatch: `App.vue` watches the whole `routeState` object and maps the landed path to a tab through `topLevelTabForPath()`, which derives the match from the single `NAV_TABS` source with exact segment comparison rather than keeping a second path list.
